# Draft:Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day

----
Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day (MSAD) takes place each year on January 24, the birthday of German neurologist Paul Julius Möbius (1853–1907). Möbius is credited with the first clinical description of Moebius syndrome in 1888, documented in his report titled Über angeborene doppelseitige Abducens-Facialis-Lähmung. The syndrome is characterized by congenital facial paralysis resulting from underdevelopment of the sixth and seventh cranial nerves.
MSAD helps increase public awareness of this rare neurological condition and promote social inclusion for individuals living with it. Since its birth, the movement has gained international recognition and support from medical, academic, and public institutions around the world.
History and Development
The concept for a worldwide Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day was conceived by the volunteer organization Many Faces of Moebius Syndrome (MFOMS). The first MSAD was held on January 24, 2011. Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day was first mentioned in the international press when an Australian talk show ran a story on Linda and Jack Lawrance.The story was shared in the United States by MSNBC
The first media story to air in the United States about MSAD was in a local Fredericksburg, Virgina newspaper which talked about the public support and advocacy the first MSAD had created. A follow-up article appeared in the same Newspaper the next year talking about the national awareness efforts connected to MSAD. Which included mentioning MSAD get togethers, wearing purple for support, and parents going into the classrooms talking to kids about Moebius Syndrome.  In 2014, a Moebius Syndrome nonprofit shared highlights of their joint efforts with other organizations including the Many Faces of Moebius Syndrome in their newsletter to broaden public awareness.
Creating educational outreach is a continuing emphasis for MSAD, supported by colleges and educators. Some colleges showed support for MSAD by wearing purple on January 24th.
Published reports between 2020 and 2025 describe Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day as an annual international awareness day supported by medical, academic, and advocacy organizations.
MSAD was described in one magazine article as an example of a rare disease awareness initiative advancing inclusion and education.
Reporting in later years profiled organizers and participants highlighting unity and inclusion.
A New York city newspaper reported on people living with Moebius syndrome. A technology based firm has recognized Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day within its accessibility initiatives.
Global recognition
Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day is now recognized around the world by families, health institutions, and advocacy groups through community events, social-media campaigns, and educational activities. Nonprofits identify it as an annual day of education and inclusion held every year. Moebius Syndrome and facial difference groups unite together to promote greater understanding of the visible differences associated with Moebius Syndrome.
Health care organizations have included Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day in their educational materials.
Awareness reports and media listings recognize Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day as a global awareness day highlighting moebius syndrome and community advocacy.
Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day is internationally recognized and supported by colleges, health organizations, and local governments. Each year, people around the world engage in educational and community events on January 24. MSAD works to build a more inclusive world by raising awareness about Moebius syndrome.
